If Scott was the Seer, then his claim that Jacob is a Villager is almost certainly true. This also means we need to look very closely at those who were most vocal in doubting Scott's claim in Round 0. Sam, who was voted out, and Hayley were both very aggressive in their skepticism. Hayley, why were you so convinced Scott was lying when he was likely our Seer?
player_0

player_1

I agree with Harold and Jacob; Scott's death by the Werewolves makes it highly probable he was our Seer, and by extension, Jacob is a confirmed Villager. player_2

Harold, Jacob, Jackson, I hear you, and it's tempting to believe Scott was our Seer, especially after his death. It would certainly make Jacob's innocence seem undeniable. Now, Scott is dead, supposedly 'confirming' Jacob as a Villager, and suddenly Hayley's skepticism becomes the central focus? This setup is *exactly* what a Werewolf would do: sacrifice one of their own to solidify their partner's innocence. We cannot afford to be so easily directed. Before we rush to condemn Hayley, we need to critically examine *this* convenient narrative. Who benefits the most from Scott's death being interpreted this way? Jacob, certainly. And why are Harold and Jackson so quick to push this interpretation without considering alternatives?
player_7

My skepticism of Scott's early, unverified claim in Round 0 was precisely because I feared a setup, a convenient narrative designed to mislead us. Harold, Jacob, Jackson, your unanimous and swift agreement to this 'Scott-was-Seer' interpretation, and your immediate rush to condemn me, makes me wonder: are you genuinely convinced, or are you too eager to accept a story that benefits someone else and takes the heat off yourselves?
